monsters.name: Bat
monsters.pageRef: Bat [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Bat (SRD 5.1); Bat (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A cave roof, belfry or hollow tree, shared with hundreds more of its kind.

description.text: A small brown insect-eater, common wherever there is a cave roof, a belfry or a hollow tree to hang from. Bats hunt on the wing in complete darkness, steering by sound, and one of them can do nothing whatever to a person. A whole roost coming out of a shaft at dusk is loud and unnerving, and that is the extent of it.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d-7 cutting, Reach C. Barely a wound; the bat is a nuisance and a disease vector, not a threat.

notes: Racial cost: -101 points of traits plus 5 points of skills.
Body weight: 1 oz.
Movement: ground Move 2; air Move 12 (primary).
A bat on the floor drags itself. The ground Move is not a misprint.

monsters.name: Blood Hawk
monsters.pageRef: Blood Hawk [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Blood Hawk (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A stick nest on a cliff ledge, ringed with the bones of whatever the flock last brought down.

description.text: Red-eyed raptors with none of a hawk's caution. They hunt in flocks over open ground and will mob anything warm-blooded that crosses it, five or six arriving together and all going for the same face. Travelers who meet a flock in the open tend to lose an eye rather than a life.

attacks.name: Talons
attacks.notes: Talons (15): 1d-4 cutting, Reach C. Struck on the stoop, at the eyes and scalp. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Beak
attacks.notes: Beak (15): 1d-6 piercing, Reach C.

notes: Racial cost: -81 points of traits plus 2 points of skills.
Body weight: 3.5 lb.
Movement: ground Move 2; air Move 12, 18 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.lair: A wet crevice under a rock at the tide line.

description.text: A shore crab the size of a dinner plate, sidling out of the rocks to strip whatever the tide left behind. The shell is genuinely hard for something this small and the pincers hurt, but neither adds up to a fight. Fishermen boil them.

Body weight: 14 oz.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary); water Move 5.
A carapace is shell rather than hide. A scratch that would slip past thick skin does not slip past this.

monsters.name: Crocodile
monsters.pageRef: Crocodile [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Crocodile (SRD 5.1); Crocodile (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A mud bank above a slow river, with a scraped nest hollow and a slide worn down into the water.

description.text: Thirteen feet of armored reptile lying in the shallows, looking exactly like a waterlogged log. It takes prey at the water's edge, drags it under and drowns it, and its hide turns a spear that would go through anything short of a dragon. On land it is slow enough to outrun. In the water it is not losing.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 2d-2 cutting, Reach C. Closes and holds; the crocodile does not let go to bite again.

attacks.name: Death Roll
attacks.notes: Death Roll: Reach C. Against a target it already has in its jaws, the crocodile rolls its whole body. No attack roll; the victim rolls ST or DX to break the grip or is dragged under and drowned.

notes: Racial cost: -28 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Body weight: 750 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5; water Move 5, 7 at a sprint (primary).

notes: Racial cost: -158 points of traits plus 5 points of skills.

monsters.pageRef: Giant Crab [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Giant Crab (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A flooded sea cave or sunken wreck, floored with cracked shell and picked bone.

notes: Racial cost: -33 points of traits plus 6 points of skills.

Movement: ground Move 5 (primary); water Move 5.

monsters.pageRef: Giant Lizard [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Giant Lizard (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A rock cleft or cave mouth warmed by the afternoon sun, littered with shed skin.

description.text: A monitor grown to the length of a horse, tasting the air with a forked tongue and climbing a cave wall as readily as it crosses the floor. attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (14): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: -46 points of traits plus 16 points of skills.

Movement: ground Move 6 (primary).

monsters.name: Giant Sea Horse
monsters.pageRef: Giant Sea Horse [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Giant Sea Horse (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: Kelp forest and reef shallows, anchored by the tail to whatever holds still.

description.text: Sea elves and sahuagin both ride these, and a good one costs more than a good horse. It is armored in bony rings, placid to the point of stubbornness, and slower than most things that would like to eat it. Handled well it will carry a rider all day. Handled badly it simply stops.

attacks.name: Ram
attacks.notes: Ram (13): 1d+2 crushing, Reach C. Driven with the whole body; the armored snout is the only part of it built to hit anything.

notes: Racial cost: -39 points of traits plus 1 point of skills.
Body weight: 400 lb.
Movement: ground Move 3; water Move 3 (primary).

monsters.pageRef: Giant Shark [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Giant Shark (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: None; it holds a stretch of open water and patrols it.

description.text: Twenty feet of shark that has stopped regarding boats as too large to try. It comes up from below and behind, takes one bite, then circles while the target bleeds. The skin is rough enough to take the hide off a hand that grabs it.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (13): 4d-2 cutting, Reach C. Rows of serrated teeth on jaws wide enough to take a rower and his oar together.

notes: Racial cost: 57 points of traits plus 8 points of skills.
Body weight: 4,000 lb.

monsters.pageRef: Giant Toad [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane birds, fish and aquatic animals; answers Giant Toad (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A wallow under a rotting log at the edge of standing water.

description.text: A toad the size of a hound, sitting so still among the reeds that it reads as a stone until the tongue comes out. attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d-2 crushing, Reach C. The toad swallows what it can and works on the rest.

attacks.name: Tongue
attacks.notes: Tongue (14): 1d-3 crushing, Reach C,1. Lashes out a hex, sticks, and drags a lighter target into reach of the mouth.

attacks.name: Toxic Skin
attacks.notes: Toxic Skin: Reach C. Anything that bites or grapples the toad bare-handed rolls HT or is nauseated and blurred of vision for minutes. No attack roll; contact alone does it.

notes: Racial cost: -44 points of traits plus 12 points of skills.
Body weight: 200 lb.
Movement: ground Move 6 (primary); water Move 6.

description.text: A waist-high bush that has been given a mind and, unluckily for it, a clear understanding of its position. It talks, it remembers who planted it, and it cannot defend itself against anybody with an axe. Most awakened shrubs end up as somebody's informant.

attacks.name: Rake
attacks.notes: Rake (8): 1d-5 cutting, Reach C. Thorns dragged across whatever is in reach. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: 0 points of traits plus 1 point of skills.
Body weight: 45 lb.
Movement: ground Move 2 (primary).
An awakened plant is awake in the full sense and will hold a conversation, which is generally why it is in the scene at all.
Fire is the obvious answer to it. There is no vulnerability on the stat block, so a GM should rule that at the table.

monsters.pageRef: Black Dragon Wyrmling [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: dragon age and color variants; answers Black Dragon Wyrmling (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A flooded cavern behind a waterfall or under a drowned ruin, reached by swimming.

description.text: Black dragons keep to swamp and drowned ruin. They are the meanest of the chromatic line — cruel without needing a reason, patient about it, content to let a place rot around them. The breath is acid, and it goes on working after it lands. A wyrmling is newly out of the shell and already the size of a warhorse. It has a full set of teeth and no judgement at all about when to use them.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d+1 impaling, Reach C,1. Teeth built to punch through bone and hold.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (14): 1d+3 cutting, Reach C,1. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (12): 1d+2 crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Wing Buffet
attacks.notes: Wing Buffet (12): 1d+1 crushing, Reach C,2. A wing swept across the front arc, using the wings the creature's Flight already pays for. Knocks a lighter target down rather than wounding it. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Acid Breath
attacks.notes: Acid Breath (14): 3d corrosion, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of acid that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

notes: Racial cost: 304 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Body weight: 450 lb.
Movement: ground Move 4; air Move 12, 18 at a sprint (primary); water Move 4.
Immunity to its own element covers that one damage type and nothing else, and it is not in the published DR. A red dragon is not armored against a sword by being immune to fire.

The breath costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, and a dragon that could breathe every turn would be a different fight. The published rating does not yet discount it for that, so it runs high for the sixteen colors whose breath is their best attack, worst for the acid breathers. Read these dragons as somewhat less dangerous than the number says.

monsters.lair: A tunnel system dug under desert rock, with the hoard at the bottom of a sand-drowned shaft.

description.text: Blue dragons burrow under desert and hunt by lying beneath the sand until something walks over them. They are vain, orderly and territorial, and they collect gems where other dragons collect coin. The breath is a bolt of lightning down a straight line. An adult has held its territory for centuries and knows every road and every lord in it. It worked out long ago what it would do if adventurers ever turned up, and none of what happens next is improvised.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 6d-1 impaling, Reach C,1. Teeth built to punch through bone and hold.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (12): 6d+1 cutting, Reach C,1. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (10): 6d crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Wing Buffet
attacks.notes: Wing Buffet (10): 6d-1 crushing, Reach C,2. A wing swept across the front arc, using the wings the creature's Flight already pays for. Knocks a lighter target down rather than wounding it. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Lightning Breath
attacks.notes: Lightning Breath (12): 10d burning, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of lightning that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

attacks.name: Frightful Presence
attacks.notes: Frightful Presence: Reach Ranged, 20. Everyone who can see the dragon rolls Will. On a failure they are frightened of it and cannot willingly close, and a bad failure means they run. No attack roll and no defense; it costs the dragon nothing.

notes: Racial cost: 670 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Body weight: 6.5 tons.
Movement: ground Move 4; air Move 12, 24 at a sprint (primary).
Immunity to its own element covers that one damage type and nothing else, and it is not in the published DR. A red dragon is not armored against a sword by being immune to fire.

The breath costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, and a dragon that could breathe every turn would be a different fight. The published rating does not yet discount it for that, so it runs high for the sixteen colors whose breath is their best attack, worst for the acid breathers. Read these dragons as somewhat less dangerous than the number says.
Extra Attack: an adult dragon bites and claws in the same turn, which is most of what makes it different from a very large animal.

monsters.pageRef: Ancient Brass Dragon [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: dragon age and color variants; answers Ancient Brass Dragon (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A sun-warmed ruin half-buried in dune, chosen for the view and the acoustics.

description.text: Brass dragons would genuinely rather talk. One will hold a traveler in conversation for hours before letting them go, or before deciding not to, and it has centuries of gossip to get through. The breath is fire, and it comes out only after the conversation has failed. An ancient dragon is older than the kingdom it sleeps under and has outlived everyone who knew where it was. What follows is less a fight than a negotiation, conducted by something that worked out what the party wants, and what they will give up to get it, some while before they arrived.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (11): 8d-1 impaling, Reach C,1. Teeth built to punch through bone and hold.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (11): 8d+1 cutting, Reach C,1. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (9): 8d crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Wing Buffet
attacks.notes: Wing Buffet (9): 8d-1 crushing, Reach C,2. A wing swept across the front arc, using the wings the creature's Flight already pays for. Knocks a lighter target down rather than wounding it. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Fire Breath
attacks.notes: Fire Breath (11): 15d burning, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of fire that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

attacks.name: Frightful Presence
attacks.notes: Frightful Presence: Reach Ranged, 20. Everyone who can see the dragon rolls Will. On a failure they are frightened of it and cannot willingly close, and a bad failure means they run. No attack roll and no defense; it costs the dragon nothing.

notes: Racial cost: 755 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Body weight: 22 tons.
Movement: ground Move 4; air Move 12, 36 at a sprint (primary).
Immunity to its own element covers that one damage type and nothing else, and it is not in the published DR. A red dragon is not armored against a sword by being immune to fire.

The breath costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, and a dragon that could breathe every turn would be a different fight. The published rating does not yet discount it for that, so it runs high for the sixteen colors whose breath is their best attack, worst for the acid breathers. monsters.lair: Somewhere unlikely and beautiful, kept plain, with the hoard behind a door it does not bother to lock.

description.text: Gold dragons are the ones the stories are actually about: wise, formal, and perfectly willing to end a threat rather than negotiate with it. They ask questions a party would rather not answer honestly. The breath is fire, and it comes out last. A young dragon still has its growth ahead of it and none of its confidence. That combination is what gets a village burned over an insult nobody meant.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (13): 4d-2 impaling, Reach C,1. Teeth built to punch through bone and hold.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (13): 4d cutting, Reach C,1. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (11): 4d-1 crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Wing Buffet
attacks.notes: Wing Buffet (11): 4d-2 crushing, Reach C,2. A wing swept across the front arc, using the wings the creature's Flight already pays for. Knocks a lighter target down rather than wounding it. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Fire Breath
attacks.notes: Fire Breath (13): 6d burning, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of fire that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

attacks.name: Frightful Presence
attacks.notes: Frightful Presence: Reach Ranged, 20. Everyone who can see the dragon rolls Will. On a failure they are frightened of it and cannot willingly close, and a bad failure means they run. No attack roll and no defense; it costs the dragon nothing.

notes: Racial cost: 492 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Body weight: 2,600 lb.
Movement: ground Move 4; air Move 12, 24 at a sprint (primary); water Move 4.
Immunity to its own element covers that one damage type and nothing else, and it is not in the published DR. A red dragon is not armored against a sword by being immune to fire.

The breath costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, and a dragon that could breathe every turn would be a different fight. The published rating does not yet discount it for that, so it runs high for the sixteen colors whose breath is their best attack, worst for the acid breathers. Read these dragons as somewhat less dangerous than the number says.

They are likelier than any other dragon to simply help, and people who impose on that goodwill do it once. The breath is a cone of killing cold. An ancient dragon is older than the kingdom it sleeps under and has outlived everyone who knew where it was. What follows is less a fight than a negotiation, conducted by something that worked out what the party wants, and what they will give up to get it, some while before they arrived.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (11): 8d-1 impaling, Reach C,1. Teeth built to punch through bone and hold.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (11): 8d+1 cutting, Reach C,1. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (9): 8d crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Wing Buffet
attacks.notes: Wing Buffet (9): 8d-1 crushing, Reach C,2. A wing swept across the front arc, using the wings the creature's Flight already pays for. Knocks a lighter target down rather than wounding it. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Cold Breath
attacks.notes: Cold Breath (11): 15d burning, Reach Ranged, cone. A cone of freezing cold that catches everything in front of the dragon. It costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, which is the only reason a fight with one lasts more than a turn.

attacks.name: Frightful Presence
attacks.notes: Frightful Presence: Reach Ranged, 20. Everyone who can see the dragon rolls Will. On a failure they are frightened of it and cannot willingly close, and a bad failure means they run. No attack roll and no defense; it costs the dragon nothing.

notes: Racial cost: 755 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Body weight: 22 tons.
Movement: ground Move 4; air Move 12, 36 at a sprint (primary).
Immunity to its own element covers that one damage type and nothing else, and it is not in the published DR. A red dragon is not armored against a sword by being immune to fire.

The breath costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second, and a dragon that could breathe every turn would be a different fight. The published rating does not yet discount it for that, so it runs high for the sixteen colors whose breath is their best attack, worst for the acid breathers. Read these dragons as somewhat less dangerous than the number says.
Extra Attack: it bites and claws in the same turn, which is most of what makes it different from a very large animal.

attacks.name: Shield Bash

notes: Racial cost: 98 points of traits plus 16 points of skills.

description.text: Horse from the withers back, person from the withers up, and entirely one animal about it — a centaur does not ride, it runs. attacks.name: Hooves

notes: Racial cost: 173 points of traits plus 22 points of skills.

Movement: ground Move 7, 14 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Gnoll
monsters.pageRef: Gnoll [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Gnoll (SRD 5.1); Gnoll (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: Whatever was standing there before the pack arrived, now roofless and stinking.

description.text: Hyena-headed raiders who hunt in packs and take the long way around to come in behind. Gnolls will follow a scent for days, they are audibly delighted by a fight going their way, and they stop to eat before it is properly over. A camp they have been through can be found from a long way off by smell.

attacks.name: Battleaxe
attacks.notes: Battleaxe (12): 2d+1 cutting, Reach 1. Taken off somebody, kept badly, and still perfectly effective.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C. Used the moment the target is down, and often instead of finishing the fight.

attacks.name: Shortbow
attacks.notes: Shortbow (11): 1d+1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 100. Loosed at anything running away. The damage is the bow's.

notes: Racial cost: 80 points of traits plus 22 points of skills.
Body weight: 250 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).

monsters.name: Goblin
monsters.pageRef: Goblin [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Goblin (SRD 5.1); Goblin (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A warren behind somebody else's ruin, entered through a hole cut too small for a man in mail.

description.text: Small, sour and numerous. One goblin is a nuisance and runs at the first real hit. Twelve of them in a tunnel they dug themselves, with spears and a hole in the ceiling, are a serious afternoon. They are not brave and they know it, so they do not fight anywhere they have not arranged in advance.

attacks.name: Shortsword
attacks.notes: Shortsword (12): 1d-1 cutting, Reach 1. Notched, too big for the hand holding it, and swung anyway.

attacks.name: Spear
attacks.notes: Spear (12): 1d-1 impaling, Reach 1,2. The one goblin weapon that works, because it lets them fight three deep from behind each other.

attacks.name: Shortbow
attacks.notes: Shortbow (11): 1d+1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 100. Loosed in volleys from a gallery nobody looked up at. The damage is the bow's.

notes: Racial cost: 10 points of traits plus 20 points of skills.
Body weight: 65 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).

monsters.name: Gray Elf
monsters.pageRef: Gray Elf [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Gray Elf (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A hall on a high valley shoulder, older than the road up to it and harder to find than either.

description.text: The high, thin, silver-haired kind, and the most insufferable. Gray elves live in mountain valleys reading things nobody else can, decline to explain themselves, and are genuinely as clever as they behave. They are also slight, and quite aware that this is why they took up magic. Spells cast at one tend to slide off.

attacks.name: Longbow
attacks.notes: Longbow (13): 1d+2 impaling, Reach Ranged, 200. A tall bow drawn to the ear. The damage is the bow's, which is why a slight archer is not a weak one.

attacks.name: Longsword
attacks.notes: Longsword (12): 1d-1 cutting, Reach 1. Worn as a matter of form for a century at a time, and still perfectly well handled.

notes: Racial cost: 79 points of traits plus 20 points of skills.
Body weight: 100 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).
The spell list is the GM's to assign. What is here is the racial template, not any particular oni's education.

monsters.pageRef: Half-Elf [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Half-Elf (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A room over a taproom in whichever town has not yet decided what to make of them.

description.text: Human enough to live in a human town and elven enough that nobody there forgets it. Half-elves get a century and a half rather than a millennium, see well by starlight, hear the conversation at the next table, and are very hard to lie to. Most of them end up as the person two communities send to talk to each other.

notes: Racial cost: 41 points of traits plus 20 points of skills.

monsters.name: Half-Orc
monsters.pageRef: Half-Orc [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Half-Orc (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A barracks, a caravan guard's tent, or the far end of whichever bar will serve them.

description.text: Stronger and tougher than a man, and treated worse than either parent's people would treat a stranger. Half-orcs make excellent soldiers and are hired as such by everyone who then declines to drink with them. The temper is real and mostly earned, and it is why the arrangement rarely lasts a season.

attacks.name: Battleaxe
attacks.notes: Battleaxe (11): 1d+4 cutting, Reach 1. Bought with the first month's wages and never replaced.

attacks.name: Punch
attacks.notes: Punch (12): 1d-1 crushing, Reach C. Thrown far more often than the axe, and usually in a room where the axe would be unwelcome.

notes: Racial cost: -14 points of traits plus 20 points of skills.
Body weight: 200 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).

monsters.name: Hobgoblin
monsters.pageRef: Hobgoblin [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Hobgoblin (SRD 5.1); Hobgoblin (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A fort with cleared ground in front of it, a watch roster, and a gate that is actually shut.

description.text: The goblinoid that got organized. Hobgoblins drill, post sentries, hold a line when it is losing and rotate the front rank while they do it, so six of them are a harder problem than twenty goblins and a much worse surprise. They are not frightened of adventurers. They have a standing plan for adventurers.

attacks.name: Longsword
attacks.notes: Longsword (13): 1d+3 cutting, Reach 1. Drilled with, maintained, and used in a line with somebody else's shield on the flank.

attacks.name: Shield Bash
attacks.notes: Shield Bash (13): 1d-1 crushing, Reach 1. The line steps forward together. This is what steps forward first.

attacks.name: Longbow
attacks.notes: Longbow (12): 1d+2 impaling, Reach Ranged, 200. Volleyed on command from the rank behind. The damage is the bow's.

notes: Racial cost: 79 points of traits plus 22 points of skills.
Body weight: 200 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).
Mail and a shield are standard issue and are not in this record's DR, so a hobgoblin met in the field is better protected than the stat block says.

monsters.pageRef: Kobold [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Kobold (SRD 5.1); Kobold (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A mine they dug themselves, in which every third corridor is a mistake to walk down.

description.text: Knee-high scaled things with dog-like snouts, and by some distance the best military engineers in any dungeon. A kobold in a fair fight is nothing. Kobolds do not have fair fights — they have pits, deadfalls, thirty of themselves, and a corridor whose safe route they know. Cold slows them and daylight makes them miserable.

attacks.name: Spear
attacks.notes: Spear (12): 1d-2 impaling, Reach 1,2. Held at the far end and used from behind whatever is in the way.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 1d-4 cutting, Reach C. What is left when the spear has been dropped and the corridor is full.

attacks.name: Sling
attacks.notes: Sling (11): 1d-3 crushing, Reach Ranged, 60. From a ledge, in the dark, at a party already dealing with something else.

notes: Racial cost: -14 points of traits plus 26 points of skills.
Body weight: 45 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).
Kobolds are reptiles. A cold gallery genuinely slows them down.

monsters.lair: A village of stilt huts over black water, reached by a channel only a flat boat clears.

description.text: Scaled, tailed and entirely at home in water a person would drown in. Lizardfolk hunt from below, hold their breath for minutes together, and come up under a boat rather than alongside it. They are not cruel and not much interested in anyone else's business, which holds exactly as long as nobody hunts their stretch of marsh.

attacks.name: Barbed Spear
attacks.notes: Barbed Spear (11): 1d+2 impaling, Reach 1,2. Fire-hardened, barbed for fish and entirely adequate for the other thing.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C. Delivered in the water, on something already being held under.

attacks.name: Tail
attacks.notes: Tail (10): 1d crushing, Reach C,2. Swept through the rear arc at knee height. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: 49 points of traits plus 22 points of skills.
Body weight: 200 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary); water Move 5.
DR 2 is scale rather than armor, so a scratch that only needs skin contact still gets through. Lizardfolk wear nothing over it.

attacks.name: Thrown Spear

notes: Racial cost: 73 points of traits plus 14 points of skills.

Movement: ground Move 5; water Move 5 (primary).

monsters.lair: A flooded sea cave with a shingle shelf at the back, and bones on the shelf.

description.text: Ogres that went into the sea and got worse. A merrow is ten feet of green-gray muscle with a harpoon and a coil of rope, and its whole method is to put the barb into somebody at the rail and pull. They are not clever. They are patient in the way an ambush predator is patient, and a wreck is what they have been waiting for.

attacks.name: Harpoon
attacks.notes: Harpoon (10): 2d+2 impaling, Reach 1,2. Barbed and roped. Being hit by it is the smaller half of the problem.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (11): 2d-2 cutting, Reach C. Taken while the harpoon rope is still being hauled.

attacks.name: Slam
attacks.notes: Slam (10): 2d-1 crushing, Reach C,1. Delivered from below with the whole mass behind it, in water, where nobody has footing.

notes: Racial cost: 84 points of traits plus 10 points of skills.
Body weight: 650 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5; water Move 5 (primary).

monsters.pageRef: Mountain Dwarf [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Mountain Dwarf (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A hold cut into a valley wall, with the forge at the front and the mine behind it.

description.text: The dwarves who stayed where the sun still reaches: hold-builders, smiths, and soldiers by inclination. A mountain dwarf finds a warm body in an unlit gallery, walks all day under a load that would fell a taller man, and holds a grudge with the same steady competence it brings to everything else. They fight in ranks and they do not give ground.

attacks.name: Warhammer
attacks.notes: Warhammer (12): 1d+4 crushing, Reach 1. Made at the forge it was carried out of, and heavier than it looks in that hand.

attacks.name: Dwarven Axe
attacks.notes: Dwarven Axe (12): 1d+3 cutting, Reach 1. The other half of the same argument.

notes: Racial cost: 52 points of traits plus 22 points of skills.
Body weight: 150 lb.
Movement: ground Move 4 (primary).
Mail and a shield are the usual kit and are not in this record's DR.

monsters.lair: A cave with a fire outside it and the remains of several carts scattered downhill.

description.text: Ten feet of appetite with a club. Ogres are slow, stupid, foul-tempered and enormously strong, and a fight with one comes down to arithmetic: sooner or later it connects, and whoever it connects with stops being a combatant. They take a toll on roads, eat what they take, and do not entertain a second offer.

attacks.name: Greatclub
attacks.notes: Greatclub (10): 3d+5 crushing, Reach 1,2. A tree limb with a stone lashed into the end. It arrives slowly and it does not matter.

attacks.name: Javelin
attacks.notes: Javelin (10): 2d impaling, Reach Ranged, 20. A sharpened fence rail, thrown downhill at whoever is fastest.

attacks.name: Fist
attacks.notes: Fist (11): 2d-1 crushing, Reach C,1. What happens when the club is on the wrong side of the fight.

notes: Racial cost: 48 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Body weight: 650 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).
DR 2 is hide. An ogre wears no armor over it, so that is the whole of its protection.

monsters.pageRef: Oni [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Oni (SRD 5.1); Ogre Mage (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A house in a mountain village where the previous family is not discussed.

description.text: An ogre with a sorcerer's education and centuries of practice at being somebody's neighbor. In its own shape it is a horned blue giant with a glaive. In the shape it usually wears it is a well-liked man in a mountain village. It flies, it vanishes, it heals whatever is done to it, and it would much rather charm the guard than fight the party.

attacks.name: Glaive
attacks.notes: Glaive (13): 4d+3 cutting, Reach 1,2. Kept on the wall of the house it took, and reached for without changing shape first.

attacks.name: Cone of Cold
attacks.notes: Cone of Cold (14): 6d burning, Reach Ranged, cone. A breath of killing cold across the front arc. It costs the oni to use and cannot be repeated every second.

attacks.name: Charm
attacks.notes: Charm: Reach Ranged, 10. One person is told to stop, and rolls against Will to not. The oni much prefers this to the glaive, because a charmed guard opens the door.

notes: Racial cost: 437 points of traits plus 40 points of skills.
Body weight: 700 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary); air Move 11.
Oni in SRD 5.1 and Ogre Mage in SRD 3.5 are one creature, and this is both. The flight comes from the older heading and is kept.
The breath costs the creature to use and cannot be repeated every second; the published rating does not yet discount it for that.

monsters.lair: A stockade round a stolen village, or a gallery in somebody else's mine.

description.text: Broad, gray-skinned and permanently furious. Orcs raid because raiding is the shape their society has settled into and because they enjoy it. They come in numbers, close immediately, and keep coming well past the point a sensible band would have withdrawn. Daylight leaves them squinting, so the attack is nearly always at dusk.

attacks.name: Falchion
attacks.notes: Falchion (12): 2d+1 cutting, Reach 1. Heavy, badly balanced and swung by an arm that does not care.

attacks.name: Javelin
attacks.notes: Javelin (11): 1d+1 impaling, Reach Ranged, 20. Thrown once at the charge, then forgotten about.

attacks.name: Fist
attacks.notes: Fist (11): 1d crushing, Reach C. Used on other orcs about as often as on anyone else.

notes: Racial cost: 7 points of traits plus 18 points of skills.
Body weight: 200 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).
Mail scraps and a shield are common and are not in this record's DR.
The camouflage and non-detection a svirfneblin can call are not on the stat block. Both come and go, and a GM should rule them.

attacks.name: Needle Sword
attacks.notes: Needle Sword (15): 1d-6 impaling, Reach C. Genuinely a threat only to something the sprite's own size, and drawn with complete confidence regardless.

notes: Racial cost: 84 points of traits plus 30 points of skills.

Movement: ground Move 2; air Move 11 (primary).

monsters.name: Cheetah
monsters.pageRef: Cheetah [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Cheetah (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A shaded scrape in tall grass where cubs are left while the mother hunts.

description.text: The fastest thing on four legs, and the least able to keep it up. A cheetah stalks to within a hundred yards, then spends everything it has in a few seconds, knocking its quarry off its feet at the end of the run. Caught at that moment it is exhausted and light-boned, and it will give up the kill rather than fight for it.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (16): 1d-2 cutting, Reach C. Aimed at the throat once the quarry is down.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (16): 1d-2 cutting, Reach C. Used to trip a running target rather than to wound. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: 18 points of traits plus 16 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 24 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Death Dog
monsters.pageRef: Death Dog [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Death Dog (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A fouled dry wash or ruin littered with the picked-over remains of travelers.

description.text: A two-headed hound the color of dust, running the dry country in pairs and hating everything that walks upright. Both heads bite and both heads watch, so there is no blind side to approach from. What kills travelers is rarely the wound. It is what grows in the wound afterwards, slowly and visibly, and it does not stop on its own.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (15): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C. Anyone bitten rolls HT. On a failure the wound will not close: it goes gray at the edges and spreads, costing 1 HP a day until the rot is cured by magic or by cutting well past the margin. The lost HP does not return until the disease is stopped.

notes: Racial cost: 38 points of traits plus 12 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6 (primary).

monsters.lair: A cave mouth or undercut bank fouled with bone, held by the whole pack.

description.text: A wolf grown to the size of a pony, hunting in packs that work a treeline the way soldiers work a hedgerow. They circle, they cut off the slowest, and they take turns. One is a serious fight. Four have already picked somebody.

monsters.name: Elk
monsters.pageRef: Elk [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Elk (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: Open woodland edge and high meadow; the herd beds where it grazes.

description.text: A deer the size of a horse, carrying a rack wide enough to catch on branches. Out of season it is meat that runs away. In the rut a bull is loud, sleepless and looking for something to fight, and a party crossing his meadow will do.

attacks.name: Antlers
attacks.notes: Antlers (12): 2d impaling, Reach C,1.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Hooves (10): 2d+2 crushing, Reach C,1. Front hooves, brought down on a target that has gone down.

notes: Racial cost: -11 points of traits plus 6 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 5, 10 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Giant Badger
monsters.pageRef: Giant Badger [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Giant Badger (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A dug sett of packed earth tunnels with several bolt holes, extended every year.

description.text: Low, wide and built entirely out of bad attitude, with digging claws that go through packed earth and will do the same to a boot. It would rather be underground than anywhere else. A party that opens up its sett gets everything the badger has, immediately, without a warning growl.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (13): 1d-2 cutting, Reach C. Digging claws, as long as a knife. Cannot parry.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (13): 1d-2 cutting, Reach C.

notes: Racial cost: -32 points of traits plus 4 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6 (primary).

monsters.name: Giant Boar
monsters.pageRef: Giant Boar [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Giant Boar (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A wallow the size of a cart, ringed by uprooted saplings and churned mud.

description.text: A boar the size of a plow horse, with hide over the shoulders that turns a spear point and a temper that has never once improved. It charges the moment it is sure, keeps going through the first wound, and is generally still coming when whoever stood the ground has reconsidered.

attacks.name: Tusks
attacks.notes: Tusks (12): 2d impaling, Reach C,1. Tusks the length of a forearm, driven upward on the charge.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 2d-1 cutting, Reach C.

notes: Racial cost: -10 points of traits plus 4 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 5, 7 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.pageRef: Giant Elk [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Giant Elk (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: Deep old forest and high valleys, far from any road.

description.text: Rare enough that seeing one counts as a sign rather than a sighting. It stands taller at the shoulder than a mounted rider, moves through heavy timber without hurrying, and watches a party with something closer to judgement than fear. Killing one is legal almost nowhere and forgiven almost never.

attacks.notes: Antlers (14): 3d-1 impaling, Reach C,2.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Hooves (12): 3d+2 crushing, Reach C,1. Against a target already down.

notes: Racial cost: 81 points of traits plus 8 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 12 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Giant Goat
monsters.pageRef: Giant Goat [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Giant Goat (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: Ledges and scree above the tree line, on ground nothing else will stand on.

description.text: An ill-tempered mountain goat the size of a pony, standing on ledges that have no business holding it. Hill folk keep them for milk and haulage and put up with the bruises. In the wild they defend a slope by ramming, and on bad footing the fall afterwards is worse than the hit.

attacks.name: Ram
attacks.notes: Ram (12): 1d+2 crushing, Reach C. Delivered downhill wherever possible.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Hooves (10): 1d+3 crushing, Reach C,1.

notes: Racial cost: -44 points of traits plus 6 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).

monsters.name: Giant Hyena
monsters.pageRef: Giant Hyena [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Giant Hyena (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A den under a thorn thicket or ruin, floored with splintered bone.

description.text: Shoulder-high, sloped from front to back, and loud in the dark. Giant hyenas run in clans and are as happy taking a kill off something else as making their own. They will follow a caravan for days without closing, waiting for somebody to fall behind. The jaws go through bone as a matter of routine.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (15): 1d+1 cutting, Reach C. Jaws built to crack marrow bone; armor straps and shield rims fare no better.

notes: Racial cost: -24 points of traits plus 8 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 9 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Giant Weasel
monsters.pageRef: Giant Weasel [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Giant Weasel (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A stolen burrow or root cavity, taken from whatever dug it and ate first.

description.text: A weasel grown to the length of a man, all spine and appetite, pouring through gaps too small to crawl through and seeing perfectly well in a lightless tunnel. Strength is not the point. It reaches the throat first and does not let go.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (16): 1d-3 impaling, Reach C. Long canines, aimed at the neck and held on.

notes: Racial cost: -21 points of traits plus 20 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6 (primary).

attacks.name: Ram
attacks.notes: Ram (11): 1d-1 crushing, Reach C.

notes: Racial cost: -110 points of traits plus 6 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).

monsters.pageRef: Horse, Heavy [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Draft Horse (SRD 5.1); Horse, Heavy (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A stable or picket line; a heavy horse is property, not wildlife.

description.text: The plow and wagon horse: heavy through the chest, slow to startle, strong enough to drag a loaded cart out of a flooded ford. It is not a fighting animal and will not carry anybody into a fight. It hauls what an expedition cannot and it eats accordingly.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Hooves (8): 3d+2 crushing, Reach C,1. Shod rear hooves; a connecting kick breaks what it lands on.

notes: Racial cost: -50 points of traits plus 2 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 5, 7 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Lion
monsters.pageRef: Lion [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Lion (SRD 5.1); Lion (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A shaded kopje or thicket the pride returns to between hunts.

description.text: A pride hunts in daylight when it suits and at night when it does not. The lionesses do the work, spread wide through grass that hides them completely until the last twenty yards, and the male arrives afterwards to take what he wants. A single lion is manageable. A pride is a flanking maneuver.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (15): 2d-2 cutting, Reach C. Closes on the throat and holds.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (15): 2d-2 cutting, Reach C. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: 7 points of traits plus 16 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 9 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Mammoth
monsters.pageRef: Mammoth [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Mammoth (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: None; the herd follows forage across tundra and cold steppe.

description.text: An elephant rebuilt for a country that freezes solid: shag-haired, high-shouldered, tusks sweeping forward until they cross. The cold does nothing to it. Herds are dangerous by accident and lethal on purpose, and the tribes that hunt them do it from a distance, with everybody they have.

attacks.name: Tusks
attacks.notes: Tusks (9): 6d impaling, Reach C,2. Curved tusks longer than a spear.

attacks.name: Trample
attacks.notes: Trample (7): 6d crushing, Reach C. Against a target already down.

notes: Racial cost: 199 points of traits plus 2 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 5, 7 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Mule
monsters.pageRef: Mule [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Mule (SRD 5.1); Mule (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: None; a mule belongs to a pack train.

description.text: The pack animal of choice anywhere a cart cannot go: stronger than a donkey, tougher than a horse, and impossible to talk into a bad idea. It carries an expedition's load up switchbacks all day, refuses a single step onto rotten ground, and kicks whoever insists.

attacks.name: Kick
attacks.notes: Kick (8): 2d+1 crushing, Reach C,1. A mule kicks sideways and backwards, and its aim is better than anyone expects.

notes: Racial cost: -28 points of traits plus 1 point of skills.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).

monsters.pageRef: Panther [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Panther (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A fork in a heavy branch above a game trail, with a kill stored in it.

description.text: A black leopard that hunts from above and is not seen beforehand. It works the canopy over a trail, drops onto whoever is walking last, and is back up the trunk with the body before the front of the column has turned around. The silence is most of the danger.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (16): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (16): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: 30 points of traits plus 24 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 9 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Saber-Toothed Tiger
monsters.pageRef: Saber-Toothed Tiger [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Saber-Toothed Tiger (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A rock shelter above a herd trail, floored with the ribs of things much larger than a person.

description.text: Heavier and slower than a tiger, and built for one job: putting something enormous on the ground and opening its throat with a pair of teeth as long as daggers. It cannot run anything down. It has already spent an hour getting close enough that it does not have to.

attacks.name: Sabre Teeth
attacks.notes: Sabre Teeth (15): 2d impaling, Reach C. Two blades of tooth, driven down into the neck once the target is pinned.

attacks.name: Claws
attacks.notes: Claws (15): 2d cutting, Reach C. Used to hold the target still. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: 29 points of traits plus 12 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 9 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.lair: A den in dense cover near water, at the center of a territory it patrols alone.

monsters.name: Warhorse, Heavy
monsters.pageRef: Warhorse, Heavy [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Warhorse (SRD 5.1); Warhorse, Heavy (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A stable, and a groom who knows better than to walk behind it.

description.text: A destrier: bred heavy, trained not to shy from fire, steel or screaming, and taught to fight from under a rider. It costs more than most people's houses and earns it, because it will carry a charge home into a line that is trying very hard to stop it. On the ground it is foul-tempered.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Hooves (12): 2d+4 crushing, Reach C,1. Trained to strike forward on command rather than only to kick out behind.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (12): 2d crushing, Reach C.

notes: Racial cost: 15 points of traits plus 4 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 12 at a sprint (primary).
The light warhorse the 3.5 corpus prints separately is this record ridden lighter; use the same statistics and drop the barding.

monsters.pageRef: Wolf [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: mundane land animals; answers Wolf (SRD 5.1); Wolf (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A dug den under a bank or root ball, used only while there are pups.

description.text: Alone, a wolf is a nervous dog with better teeth. In a pack it is a method: they test a party for a mile, find who tires, and then commit all at once from three sides. Winter packs are larger, hungrier and far less careful about what counts as prey.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d-1 cutting, Reach C. Wolves bite and pull backwards, working to drag a target off its feet.

notes: Racial cost: -25 points of traits plus 10 points of skills.
Movement: ground Move 6, 9 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Spider Swarm
monsters.pageRef: Spider Swarm [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: swarms; answers Spider Swarm (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A web-choked corner of a ruin, with an egg sac above the doorway.

description.text: An egg sac breaks and the ceiling comes down in pieces, and the pieces are moving. Individually the spiders are harmless. In these numbers they get inside armor, inside sleeves and inside the neck of a cloak, and there is nowhere to hit that does any good.

attacks.name: Swarming Bites
attacks.notes: Swarming Bites: 1d-4 impaling, Reach C. No attack roll and no defense. Roll HT against the combined venom of several hundred bites or take fever and a shaking hand for the rest of the day.

notes: Racial cost: -19 points of traits plus 0 points of skills.
Body weight: 4.5 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).

monsters.name: Swarm of Bats
monsters.pageRef: Swarm of Bats [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: swarms; answers Swarm of Bats (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A cave roof or a belfry, and the column of them that leaves it at dusk.

description.text: Hundreds of them come out of a shaft at once and fill the passage wall to wall. Nothing in the swarm can do a person much harm on its own, and that hardly matters: nobody can see, nobody can hear an order, and the torch has already gone out.

attacks.name: Swarming Bites
attacks.notes: Swarming Bites: 1d-3 cutting, Reach C. No attack roll and no defense. The bites are minor; the swarm's real effect is that anyone inside it is blinded, buffeted and unable to hold a line.

notes: Racial cost: 57 points of traits plus 0 points of skills.
Body weight: 6.5 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5; air Move 11, 16 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.name: Swarm of Insects
monsters.pageRef: Swarm of Insects [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: swarms; answers Swarm of Insects (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: Standing water, a midden, or a corpse nobody found.

description.text: Whatever the region breeds — hornets, biting flies, ants boiling up out of the ground. Armor is no help and the swarm cannot be frightened off. Anyone who needs to concentrate for a few seconds is going to have a much worse time than anyone who only needs to swing.

attacks.name: Bites and Stings
attacks.notes: Bites and Stings: 1d-2 cutting, Reach C. No attack roll and no defense. Roll HT or spend the fight swatting: any task needing concentration, and any spell, fails while the swarm is on them.

notes: Racial cost: -37 points of traits plus 0 points of skills.
Body weight: 10 lb.
Movement: ground Move 3; air Move 11 (primary).

monsters.name: Swarm of Poisonous Snakes
monsters.pageRef: Swarm of Poisonous Snakes [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: swarms; answers Swarm of Poisonous Snakes (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A den pit under a ruin, where they have wintered together for longer than the ruin has been empty.

description.text: A den's worth of vipers, disturbed all at once and coming out over each other in every direction. There is no way past them that does not involve being bitten several times, and the venom does not care that each snake delivered only a little.

attacks.name: Swarming Bites
attacks.notes: Swarming Bites: 1d-1 impaling, Reach C. No attack roll and no defense. Roll HT at a penalty for the sheer number of doses; failure means the limb goes, then the breathing does. This is the most lethal thing any of these swarms does, and it is entirely chemical.

notes: Racial cost: 21 points of traits plus 0 points of skills.
Body weight: 45 lb.
Movement: ground Move 6 (primary).

monsters.name: Swarm of Quippers
monsters.pageRef: Swarm of Quippers [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: swarms; answers Swarm of Quippers (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A warm slow reach of river that everything local knows not to cross.

description.text: The water boils. A quipper shoal takes a pack mule down to bone between one bank and the other, and anybody still in the river when it arrives has about as long as it takes to shout. Getting out is the only tactic that works.

attacks.name: Feeding Frenzy
attacks.notes: Feeding Frenzy: 1d+1 cutting, Reach C. No attack roll and no defense. Everything in the water in that hex is being bitten continuously, and blood in the water makes it worse rather than better.

notes: Racial cost: 5 points of traits plus 0 points of skills.
Body weight: 90 lb.
Movement: ground Move 6; water Move 6 (primary).

monsters.pageRef: Swarm of Rats [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: swarms; answers Swarm of Rats (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A sewer, a granary, or the space between two walls.

description.text: The classic cellar encounter, and still a real one. A rat swarm goes over a person rather than around them and does not break when hurt. What costs a party is not the bites. It is what is in them a week later.

attacks.name: Swarming Bites
attacks.notes: Swarming Bites: 1d-2 cutting, Reach C. No attack roll and no defense. Every bite is filthy: roll HT afterwards or take a fever that arrives days later, when the party is somewhere less convenient.

notes: Racial cost: -1 points of traits plus 0 points of skills.
Body weight: 65 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).
One hex of swarm.

monsters.name: Swarm of Ravens
monsters.pageRef: Swarm of Ravens [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: swarms; answers Swarm of Ravens (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A rookery in dead trees above a battlefield, a gallows, or a road with a bad reputation.

description.text: Cleverer than any other swarm by a wide margin, and the only one that appears to be making decisions. A raven flock that has decided a party is worth mobbing goes for the eyes first, breaks off when it is losing, and comes back at dusk.

attacks.name: Beaks and Claws
attacks.notes: Beaks and Claws: 1d-1 piercing, Reach C. No attack roll and no defense. Ravens go for the face and the eyes by preference: roll HT or fight blinded until the swarm is driven off.

notes: Racial cost: 76 points of traits plus 0 points of skills.
Body weight: 100 lb.
Movement: ground Move 6; air Move 12, 18 at a sprint (primary).
One hex of swarm.
Corvids plan. Play this flock as though it has an opinion about who is dangerous.

monsters.name: Skeleton
monsters.pageRef: Skeleton [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: undead template constructions, pre-materialized; answers Skeleton (SRD 5.1); Skeleton (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: Wherever it fell or was posted: a barrow passage, a crypt door, the bottom rank of somebody's cheap army.

description.text: Bones with the orders still in them. It does not tire, it does not flinch, and a blade between its ribs finds nothing there to matter. Crushing weapons end it fastest, because dry bone breaks in a way flesh does not.

attacks.name: Notched Blade
attacks.notes: Notched Blade (12): 1d+1 cutting, Reach 1. Whatever weapon it was buried or posted with, swung with no fear of the answer.

attacks.name: Claw
attacks.notes: Claw (13): 1d-2 crushing, Reach C. Finger bones driven like a handful of pegs.

notes: Racial cost: 202 points of traits plus 4 points of skills.
Body weight: 20 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).
Brittle: any major wound shatters structure. Impaling and piercing weapons find nothing worth finding, so take the injury tolerance literally.

monsters.pageRef: Minotaur Skeleton [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: undead template constructions, pre-materialized; answers Minotaur Skeleton (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A maze it no longer needs to understand to patrol.

description.text: A bull-horned frame two heads taller than a man, still walking its maze. The charge is what kills people. It does not slow into the turn, having nothing left that can pull a muscle.

attacks.name: Gore
attacks.notes: Gore (11): 2d+2 impaling, Reach C,1. The horns kept their points when everything else went.

attacks.name: Greataxe
attacks.notes: Greataxe (11): 4d+1 cutting, Reach 1,2. Swung from the shoulder joints with no muscle to slow it down between blows.

notes: Racial cost: 236 points of traits plus 2 points of skills.
Body weight: 200 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).
Brittle, like any dry-bone construction.

monsters.name: Warhorse Skeleton
monsters.pageRef: Warhorse Skeleton [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: undead template constructions, pre-materialized; answers Warhorse Skeleton (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A stable nobody mucks out, or the barrow of whoever it was buried to carry.

description.text: A rider's mount reduced to its running gear. It carries whatever it is told to carry, at a gallop it never breaks, and it does not shy — fear needed parts it no longer has.

attacks.name: Hooves
attacks.notes: Hooves (11): 2d crushing, Reach C,1. A kick with the full frame behind it and no instinct for self-preservation holding it back.

notes: Racial cost: 224 points of traits plus 1 point of skills.
Body weight: 150 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5, 10 at a sprint (primary).

monsters.pageRef: Zombie [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: undead template constructions, pre-materialized; answers Zombie (SRD 5.1); Zombie (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: Graveyard mud, plague pits, the shallow end of a necromancer's budget.

description.text: The recently dead, put back to work. One zombie is a chore for anybody with a weapon and room to move. There is never one. attacks.name: Slam
attacks.notes: Slam (9): 1d+1 crushing, Reach C. A dead weight of an arm brought down like a falling beam, and then the grip that follows it.

notes: Racial cost: 139 points of traits plus 2 points of skills.
Body weight: 150 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).

monsters.name: Ghost
monsters.pageRef: Ghost [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: undead template constructions, pre-materialized; answers Ghost (SRD 5.1); Ghost (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: The place it cannot leave: the room it died in, the road it died on, the person it died for.

description.text: Somebody still here. It drifts through the walls of the place that holds it, and the cold spot in the room is the only warning before a hand comes out of the stonework. Killing it again buys a few days. Whatever holds it here has to be dealt with for anything more.

attacks.name: Withering Touch
attacks.notes: Withering Touch (14): 1d toxic, Reach C. A hand through the chest, and the years it takes with it. Resist with HT or age visibly around the wound; armor is no answer to something that ignores the body's outside.

attacks.name: Horrifying Visage
attacks.notes: Horrifying Visage (14): 1d-4 toxic, Reach Ranged, gaze. The face it wears when it stops pretending to be what it was. A Fright Check at penalty; those who fail are staggered by terror, and the young can be aged by it.

notes: Racial cost: 566 points of traits plus 12 points of skills.
Body weight: under an ounce.
Movement: ground Move 6; air Move 12 (primary).
Whatever binds it to the site is not on the stat block. Settle that, or it comes back.

monsters.name: Vampire
monsters.pageRef: Vampire [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: undead template constructions, pre-materialized; answers Vampire (SRD 5.1); Vampire (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A defended household with money, staff who do not ask, and a windowless room nobody mentions.

description.text: A predator that owns property. It passes for a living aristocrat as long as it feeds carefully, and the household around it exists to keep the feeding careful. Sunlight burns it and it knows every hour of the almanac, so the fight on offer is the one it prepared: at night, indoors, on its ground.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (16): 1d+1 impaling, Reach C. Delivered to a grappled or willing victim. The wound is small; the draining is not, and a victim held through it loses blood by the round.

attacks.name: Slam
attacks.notes: Slam (16): 1d+3 crushing, Reach C,1. Strength far past what the frame suggests.

attacks.name: Dominating Gaze
attacks.notes: Dominating Gaze (16): 1d-4 toxic, Reach Ranged, gaze. Meet its eyes and resist with Will, or obey and remember it afterwards as a decision freely made. It prefers this to violence; violence is noisy.

notes: Racial cost: 374 points of traits plus 20 points of skills.
Body weight: 150 lb.
Movement: ground Move 6 (primary).
Sunlight does 1d per minute of exposure. Folklore's other bans — thresholds, running water, the stake — vary by telling and are the GM's to rule.
Wounds close on their own, which does not make it unkillable. Fire, beheading and daylight are the traditional ends and nothing here rules them out.

monsters.name: Lich
monsters.pageRef: Lich [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: undead template constructions, pre-materialized; answers Lich (SRD 5.1); Lich (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A tower, tomb or buried library arranged for the convenience of one scholar and the death of visitors, with its true treasure hidden somewhere else entirely.

description.text: A wizard who solved dying and went back to work. Everything about the encounter was settled before the party arrived — the approach, the ambush, which of them it wants alive to question. Destroying the body is an inconvenience. The vessel holding its life is somewhere else, and finding that is the real adventure.

attacks.name: Paralyzing Touch
attacks.notes: Paralyzing Touch (15): 1d toxic, Reach C. A hand like winter through the armor's gaps. Resist with HT or the body simply stops answering, and the lich walks past to the one it actually came for.

attacks.name: Deathly Bolt
attacks.notes: Deathly Bolt (16): 6d burning, Reach Ranged. Stated as literal dice: the bolt is a property of the lich's art, not its arm. It costs the creature to cast, and a lich in its own lair has cheaper ways to open.

attacks.name: Frightening Gaze
attacks.notes: Frightening Gaze (15): 1d-4 toxic, Reach Ranged, gaze. The full attention of something that outlived everyone's grandparents and expects to outlive their grandchildren. Fright Check at penalty; it uses this on the brave first.

notes: Racial cost: 451 points of traits plus 32 points of skills.
Body weight: 100 lb.
Movement: ground Move 6 (primary).
The stat block is the body in the room. The phylactery is not on it, and how the lich comes back is the GM's to decide.

monsters.name: Mummy Lord
monsters.pageRef: Mummy Lord [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: undead template constructions, pre-materialized; answers Mummy Lord (SRD 5.1); Mummy Lord (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: The tomb complex it was interred to rule, with its organs in jars in a chamber it defends above its own body.

description.text: The buried king still holding court. Wrapped, preserved and furious, it runs its tomb like a garrison: it knows every trap and every shortcut, its priest-craft is intact, and its fist carries a rot that turns a survivable wound into a slow sentence. It will not pursue past its borders, and it has never needed to.

attacks.name: Rotting Fist
attacks.notes: Rotting Fist (12): 2d crushing, Reach C,1. The blow lands like a club, and what it leaves behind is worse: resist with HT or take the rot, a curse under the skin. Wounds will not close and healing arts fail until the curse itself is lifted.

attacks.name: Dreadful Glare
attacks.notes: Dreadful Glare (12): 1d-4 toxic, Reach Ranged, gaze. The tomb's own verdict on trespass. Fright Check at penalty; a badly failed roll leaves the victim paralyzed by dread as it closes.

notes: Racial cost: 450 points of traits plus 16 points of skills.
Body weight: 150 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).
The rot is a curse rather than a wound. It cannot be healed until the curse is lifted, and it does not wear off with rest.

description.text: Three feet of segmented armor on forty legs, moving along a wall faster than a person walks. It hunts in the dark by touch and vibration and kills with a pair of hooked poison claws under the head. Cornering one is nearly impossible, since it simply goes wherever the wall goes.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (14): 1d-6 impaling, Reach C. The puncture is trivial. What follows is not: roll HT or take a fever, cramps and a swollen limb that is useless for hours.

notes: Racial cost: -113 points of traits plus 10 points of skills.
Body weight: 10 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).

monsters.pageRef: Giant Scorpion [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: vermin and monstrous arthropods; answers Giant Scorpion (SRD 5.1)]
monsters.lair: A scraped burrow under a slab, with the sand outside smoothed by its own passage.

description.text: Eight feet of black chitin that takes hold with the claws and takes its time with the tail. The shell turns most weapons and the pincers do not let go. The sting is what actually kills; everything before it is the scorpion arranging matters to suit itself.

attacks.name: Sting
attacks.notes: Sting (13): 1d+2 impaling, Reach C,1. Arched over the back and driven down. Roll HT or the limb goes numb, then the chest does; a second sting on a failed victim is usually the end of it.

attacks.name: Pincer
attacks.notes: Pincer (13): 1d+1 cutting, Reach C,1. Grabs and holds the target still for the sting. Cannot parry.

notes: Racial cost: -25 points of traits plus 4 points of skills.
Body weight: 250 lb.
Movement: ground Move 5 (primary).

monsters.name: Giant Spider
monsters.pageRef: Giant Spider [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: vermin and monstrous arthropods; answers Giant Spider (SRD 5.1); Monstrous Spider (SRD 3.5)]
monsters.lair: A sheet of web strung across a shaft or a stand of trees, with wrapped bundles hanging in it.

description.text: A body the size of a large dog on a ten-foot span of legs, sitting motionless at the edge of its web where the light does not reach. It reads the whole web as one sense. It wants somebody held still, and most of that was arranged before anyone thought to look up.

attacks.name: Bite
attacks.notes: Bite (15): 1d impaling, Reach C. Delivered to something already wrapped. Roll HT or go slack — the venom is meant to stop prey struggling, not to kill it outright.

attacks.name: Web
attacks.notes: Web: Reach 5. Thrown as a sheet from ambush. No damage; the target is stuck fast and must win a Quick Contest against the web's ST to tear free, and everything the spider does afterwards is against a target that cannot move. The web itself has DR 3 and can be cut or burned free; fire clears a hex of it in a turn and is by far the fastest answer.

notes: Racial cost: 8 points of traits plus 12 points of skills.
Body weight: 200 lb.
Movement: ground Move 6 (primary).
The 3.5 corpus prints 'Monstrous Spider' as a family of sizes rather than one creature; this record is the size that matches the 5.1 giant spider.
